body:
When you say "the latest version", are you saying that previous versions didn't have this problem? Or just that you're using the latest version?

I haven't run into this, but then again, I've never run ESLint on that many files. 

For comparison, can you run JSHint on the same set of files and see what happens?

Sorry, haven't done any more of that narrowing down because any time I put into this issue is still just trying to figure out how to do basic memory profiling. node-inspector is hopeless, it doesn't work with the latest devtools updates so it only allows step-through debugging. node-memwatch works but doesn't have enough information to make any useful conclusions. node-heapdump generates a useful heap dump that can be viewed in devtools but on OS X it refuses to generate more than one dump no matter how or how many times it's called. Which is frustrating because I might be able to find the issue with just two. On Windows I am still trying to get it to even compile. All of these tools are very outdated. I'm still baffled how scant and unmaintained the open-source Node.js profiling tools are.

Will continue to look into this when I get time.

Can you just run JSHint on the same directory and see what happens? That
would at least give us a ballpark.​

![](http://cs406221.vk.me/g40809365/a_d70ea455.jpg)

I've found out how to generate multiple node-heapdump snapshots. You need python 2.7, Visual Studio 2010 (Express works), node, npm, node-gyp, and then build node-heapdump on Windows, and then it works fine. So, now I can finally track this down, right?

Wrong. The other good news is that this problem magically disappeared. With the latest master branch, memory usage no longer climbs to >=1.5gb but oscillates between 100-300mb, seemingly with no (or trivial) retaining.

I will not try to track this down anymore right now, since it was really just a practical issue for me - I literally couldn't run it. Sometime in the future I could run various releases of eslint to see if and where it's a problem, and also compare to jshint, if you want me to @nzakas. Not for a while though, I've spent too many hours on this already.
Hooray for bugs that fix themselves!​

Pasting in some info from the mailing list:

I just set up an ignore file to bypass all libs.  Still getting this error, now on a different file:

```
  eslint:cli-engine Processing chooser-frontend_trunk/chooser-frontend/public/t8/min/no_NO/t8-chooser.min.js +12s
  eslint:cli-engine Linting /home/jgourgou/Documents/workspace/netrepo/chooser-frontend_trunk/chooser-frontend/public/t8/min/no_NO/t8-chooser.min.js +0ms
  eslint:cli-engine Processing chooser-frontend_trunk/chooser-frontend/public/t8/min/zh_TW/t8-dateFormatter.min.js +6s
  eslint:cli-engine Linting /home/jgourgou/Documents/workspace/netrepo/chooser-frontend_trunk/chooser-frontend/public/t8/min/zh_TW/t8-dateFormatter.min.js +0ms
FATAL ERROR: CALL_AND_RETRY_2 Allocation failed - process out of memory
```

Is there a way I can print out the size of the result object?

-Jim G

Looks like it's dying while trying to parse Highcharts.js:

```
  eslint:cli-engine Processing chooser-frontend_trunk/chooser-frontend/public/scmp/lib/highcharts/2.3.3/highcharts.js +3s
  eslint:cli-engine Linting /home/jgourgou/Documents/workspace/netrepo/chooser-frontend_trunk/chooser-frontend/public/scmp/lib/highcharts/2.3.3/highcharts.js +0ms
FATAL ERROR: CALL_AND_RETRY_2 Allocation failed - process out of memory
```

However, if I point it at that file specifically and singly:

```
eslint -c ~/.eslintrc -f compact  /home/jgourgou/Documents/workspace/netrepo/chooser-frontend_trunk/chooser-frontend/public/scmp/lib/highcharts/2.3.3/highcharts.js
```

...it executes normally, finding 2637 problems, so I'm leaning towards your first hypothesis (result object growing too large).

Thanks!

Oh wow, that's pretty big. :)

Can you try running ESLint with some debug flags?

```
$ DEBUG=eslint:cli-engine eslint .
```

(replace eslint . with whatever you use normally)

That should tell you the last file linted before the error occurs. Can you see if there's anything special about that file (size, mostly).

My two theories are:
1. It's the size of the result object growing too large.
2. It's the size of the AST for an overly large file.

So if you can get back with what the offending file looks like size-wise, we can go from there.

Apologies.  Forgot to use the -L option on my find command.

Number of (nested) subdirectories: 1063 (some of these are symlinks)
Number of files: 5809
No files over 685k

-Jim G

I don't think this is a node issue, because JSHint works fine over the same directories.

Number of (nested) subdirectories: 37  (some of these are symlinks)
Number of files: 229
No files over 250k

FWIW, I just updated to v0.13.0 and am still seeing this.

Thanks!
-Jim G

We don't have a known limit on number of files or file size, but Node.js itself does.

From what I've read, the most likely cause is a single large file. Do you have any files that are larger than a megabyte or two?

Are there any other statistics you can share about your project folder? Number of subdirectories or files?

It's this same issue.  https://github.com/eslint/eslint/issues/957  FWIW I'm running v0.12.0 on an 8 core Linux box with 64G of memory.

Thanks,
-Jim G

When I throw ESLint at a large project folder, I'm getting "FATAL ERROR: CALL_AND_RETRY_2 Allocation failed - process out of memory" errors.  Does ESLint have a maximum number of files/errors it can handle?
My hunch is that the size of the result set is growing because of the AST node reference we keep on it.

@Jimgskoop can you try the issue957 branch and see if that works for you? The tests are all exploding at the moment because I removed the AST node from results, but we can deal with that if it fixes the issue.
If the size of the result set turns out to be the issue, fixing #1098 could be an alternative solution.
@btmills That doesn't actually solve the problem. It only changes how results are output, not how the results are stored.

@nzakas I've got the issue957 code and am running it right now on my ginormous test case.  Looks like it's working!

"898918 problems"

Okay. So it looks like what was going on is that we were keeping the AST of each file in memory due to attaching a node to each message. We don't really need that node, so it's probably safe to remove it. We'll need to change how eslint-tester works since it relies on the node, but that's okay.

The `node` is really only used by ESLintTester to verify the correct node was passed into `report()`. However, we really only check the node type, so I can just attach a new `nodeType` property to the result and use that instead.
